reference.title: Cable Low Fly
reference.listing: Video (movement reference; the page could not be fetched from the authoring environment, so the data sheet was not read and the movement was taken from the exercise name and standard coaching)

breathing.pattern: Breathe in as the hands lower and open, breathe out as you sweep them up and together.
breathing.cadence: About 2.2 s down, short stretch, about 1.5 s up

prescription.effort: Stop 1-3 reps short of failure (RIR 1-3, clinical opinion)
prescription.load: Cable stack load is user-chosen: pick a weight you can sweep up to chest height with the elbow bend unchanged and without leaning back.
prescription.progression: Add reps, then one plate on each stack; slower opening

cues.text: Stand between two towers with the pulleys at the bottom, a D-handle in each hand, feet hip width, chest up; hands together in front of the upper chest, palms up, elbows softly bent.
Breathe in and let the cables draw the hands down and out in a wide arc, elbow bend fixed.
Stop with the hands out beside the hips, palms forward, and a light stretch across the chest.
Breathe out and scoop the handles up and together in front of the upper chest, as if lifting a big bowl.
Squeeze with the hands just apart at about chin to upper-chest height; shoulders down.

mistakes.mistake: Curling the handles up with the biceps
mistakes.fix: Keep the same soft elbow bend; the arm moves from the shoulder.

mistakes.mistake: Leaning back to heave the handles
mistakes.fix: Brace with a slight forward lean and lighten the stacks.
Stop at upper-chest height with the shoulders down.

mistakes.mistake: Letting the hands drift behind the body at the bottom
mistakes.fix: Stop with the hands beside the hips, a little in front of the body line.

kinematics.norm: Fixed soft bend of about 20-30 degrees (as in the dumbbell fly protocol of Solstad 2020)
From the hands out beside the hips up and in to the upper chest: a low-to-high line of pull (clinical opinion)
Palms forward at the bottom, turning up at the top (clinical opinion)
One cable per hand from its own low pulley (clinical opinion)
Upright or slightly forward, braced and still (clinical opinion)
Controlled, about 2 s down and 1.5 s up (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual, Cable Low Fly, video (movement reference)

Solstad, Andersen, Shaw, Hoel, Vonheim and Saeterbakken 2020, a comparison of muscle activation between barbell bench press and dumbbell flyes in resistance-trained males (J Sports Sci Med 19(4):645-651; PMC7675616)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, numbness or tingling occurs.
The cable load is user-chosen: pick a weight you can lift to chest height without leaning back or shrugging.
Pick the handles up from the low pulleys one at a time with a flat back, bending the knees, then step into position.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Shoulder discomfort: keep the hands lower at the top, about mid-chest.
Balance: use a staggered stance with one foot forward.
regressions: Band low-to-high fly anchored under the feet.
progressions: Slower lowering with a 1 s pause in the stretch.
Single-arm low fly for an anti-rotation challenge.

muscleNotes.pec_r: Prime mover: the upper (clavicular) fibres lift and draw the arm across the body on the low-to-high path (clinical opinion; fly mechanics as in Solstad 2020).
muscleNotes.pec_l: Prime mover: the upper (clavicular) fibres lift and draw the arm across the body on the low-to-high path (clinical opinion; fly mechanics as in Solstad 2020).
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Lifts the arm forward and up with the upper chest.
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_l: Lifts the arm forward and up with the upper chest.
muscleNotes.biceps_r: Holds the soft elbow bend and assists shoulder flexion with the palm up.
muscleNotes.biceps_l: Holds the soft elbow bend and assists shoulder flexion with the palm up.
muscleNotes.serratus_r: Rotates the shoulder blade upward as the arm rises.
muscleNotes.serratus_l: Rotates the shoulder blade upward as the arm rises.
muscleNotes.triceps_r: Keeps the elbow from bending further.
muscleNotes.triceps_l: Keeps the elbow from bending further.
muscleNotes.upper_traps_r: Steadies the shoulder girdle; should not shrug.
muscleNotes.upper_traps_l: Steadies the shoulder girdle; should not shrug.
muscleNotes.core: Keeps the trunk from leaning back as the cables pull down and out.

phases.label: Hands together at the upper chest
